AUDIT: FAIL
Objective Understood: Reviewed worker task 'sweep-adopt-veridian-scripts-401-fix-progress-completion-gate-exclude-pyt' (risk tier: tier1) by reading the actual diff, not a self-report.
Standards Reviewed: AGENTS.md Operating Rule 7c structured audit protocol; risk-tier.py's deterministic tier classification.
Scope Confirmed:  ...442-stop-the-directive-resubmission-flood-po.md | 82 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 progress_completion_gate.py                        | 55 ++++++++++++++-
 tests/test_progress_completion_gate.py             | 40 +++++++++++
 3 files changed, 175 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
Evidence Recorded: The investigative work (root-causing the stale directive-resubmission-flood premise) is solid and honestly reported, and the diff correctly stays out of tier2 territory (no migrations/schema/sql/auth/permission/security paths, no .github/workflows/** changes). However the actual code fix in progress_completion_gate.py has a real regex bug: _CLI_INVOCATION_RE's alternation (?:python3?|bash|sh) has no leading word boundary, so it matches "sh" as a bare suffix of ordinary English words (smash, polish, finish, establish, wish, publish, refresh, flash, trash, crash, cash, dash, hash, ...) immediately followed by a path ending in .py/.sh -- verified concretely, e.g. "we need to smash /opt/veridian/scripts/resource_governor.py to fix the bug" and "the real fix should establish /opt/veridian/scripts/baz.py new behavior" both spuriously match as if they were real python3/bash/sh CLI invocations. This makes the new exclusion far broader than intended (a filename genuinely following a real interpreter invocation) and broader than the diff's own three new tests exercise (all use literal 'python3 <path>' forms only, none probe the word-boundary gap). Since extract_named_code_files() feeds directly into check_completion()'s decision to skip gate enforcement entirely when no named code file remains, this bug can cause the completion gate to silently accept a 'no code needed' self-report for a genuinely-required code change whenever the SPEC's only distinguishing mention of the target file happens to sit after a word ending in 'sh' -- a realistic occurrence in this codebase's prose-heavy dispatch SPECs, and a materially larger blind spot than the four prior exclusions in this file (each scoped to a fixed boilerplate-tool allowlist or an unambiguous tool-output/citation format, not an unanchored regex that can match mid-word). This is a correctness defect in a component whose sole job is gating whether an autonomous 'no code needed' self-report is trusted for tier1 auto-merge, so it should be fixed (e.g. anchor the interpreter alternation with a real leading boundary) and re-tested before merge. Issues found: _CLI_INVOCATION_RE in progress_completion_gate.py (added ~line 287) lacks a leading word boundary before the (?:python3?|bash|sh) alternation, so it matches 'sh' as a suffix of ordinary words (smash/polish/finish/establish/wish/publish/refresh/flash/trash/crash/...) immediately followed by a .py/.sh path -- verified live with reproducible examples, e.g. 'please polish /opt/veridian/scripts/foo.py before merging' matches as a fake CLI invocation and would incorrectly exclude foo.py from the completion gate's required-file set.; None of the 3 new tests in tests/test_progress_completion_gate.py probe this word-boundary gap -- all use literal 'python3 <path>' text, so the bug ships undetected by the diff's own test coverage.; Net effect: this change can widen the completion gate's false-negative surface (silently accepting a doc-only diff for an objective that genuinely named a code file) beyond what the PR's stated intent and prior precedent in this file (narrow boilerplate-tool allowlist / unambiguous citation formats) established -- a real regression risk in a tier1-auto-mergeable safety gate.
Severity Classified: medium
Verdict: fail
Corrective Action Owner: Worker to address the findings listed above and resubmit.
Re-Audit Scheduled: Required after corrective changes are pushed.
